note: Output formats as DATA, not as a hand-kept table. Same principle as the language layer: the machine queries rows, it does not read prose. A new format is a new row here — no code change, no prompt edit. Brand- or channel-specific variants override by key.

formats.name: Short-form
formats.what: The punchy one. Scroll-stopper, one idea, out.
formats.form: A few short sentences. Hard first line. No wind-up, no build.
formats.opens_with: the sharpest single line the argument contains
formats.reads_as: someone saying one true thing and stopping

formats.name: Caption / Meta primary text
formats.what: The words above the creative in the feed.
formats.form: Real sentences. First line stands alone, then short paragraphs, one idea each, blank line between.
formats.opens_with: a line that works with the creative not yet seen
formats.reads_as: something a person typed, not something a brand approved

formats.name: Long-form story
formats.what: A story that earns its length — the middle included, not skipped.
formats.form: Paragraphs. Full prose. A reader who stops for it finishes it.
formats.opens_with: a promise the length will be worth it
formats.reads_as: a post someone wrote because they wanted to

formats.name: Social proof
formats.what: Built on other people's words — what customers actually said.
formats.form: Quotes on their own lines, connective sentences between them.
formats.opens_with: the strongest quote, or the claim the quotes will settle
formats.requires: real sourced verbatims — this format cannot be written without them

scope: Copy STYLES only — HOW the copy is written: short-form, long-form story, social proof. This is NOT the surface bank (WHERE the words go — headline, description, hook line), which is format-bank.json in this folder and a different axis entirely. A tool needing a slot reads format-bank.json; a tool needing a voice reads this. The model: components/naming/MODEL.md
